criterion_notes.c1: Examines community/settlement-part (colony) access to piped water (water mains) and sanitation infrastructure (sewerage/drainage mains) across segregated Roma habitats in Hungary.
criterion_notes.c2: Fails both the plain wording and the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading of Criterion 2. Under the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading, the study examines no rule-type mechanism governing water or sanitation service access (such as eligibility screening, administrative burden, documentation or tenure requirements, tariff/cost-recovery rules, official discretion, enforcement, or utility regulatory structure). Under the plain broad wording of Criterion 2, the study likewise examines no legal, administrative, institutional, regulatory, or governance factor affecting water or sanitation access: mentions of a 1997 governmental decree commissioning data collection, national census ethnic self-identification rules, and local minority self-governments concern ethnic population enumeration and participatory survey methodology rather than governance of water or sanitation services.
criterion_notes.c3: Contains primary empirical data from a three-phase nationwide environmental mapping survey (2000, 2002-2003, 2005) covering all 3,145 settlements in 19 counties of Hungary and characterizing 758 segregated colonies.
criterion_notes.c4: Reports colony-level infrastructure availability outcomes, specifically the prevalence of lack of sewerage/drainage and lack of piped water mains across the 758 identified colonies (Figure 3), as well as a 10-point composite score incorporating these indicators.
criterion_notes.c5: Population (758 segregated colonies with ~134,000 inhabitants across 3,145 settlements, unit of analysis: colony and county), service availability outcomes (lack of water mains and lack of sewerage), and cross-sectional survey design are identifiable, but no legal, administrative, or governance exposure variable governing water or sanitation access is examined in this descriptive environmental survey.

evidence_quotes.quote: Most frequent environmental problems in the colonies were found to be lack of sewage and gas mains, garbage deposits, waterlogged soil and lack of water mains.

This paper describes the method of the survey so as to give an example for environmental and housing data collection that other countries with sizable Roma or other disadvantaged minority populations can utilize.
availability of public utilities (electricity, piped water, gas, drainage, telephone line); environmental danger: legal or illegal waste deposit, deposit for animal carcasses, waterlogged soil, etc.

evidence_quotes.quote: All 3145 settlements of all 19 counties of Hungary were surveyed except the capital.
The most frequent environmental problems in the colonies were lack of sewerage and gas mains, the presence of garbage deposits and waterlogged soil (figure 3).

raw_response.exposure: None for service access (descriptive environmental survey of physical conditions in segregated colonies and methodological comparison of participatory vs. census/minority self-government population estimates; no legal, administrative, or governance exposure governing water or sanitation access is analysed)
raw_response.outcome: Colony-level availability of piped water (lack of water mains) and sanitation infrastructure (lack of sewerage/drainage), reported as colony-level prevalence percentages (Figure 3) and as binary components of a 10-point composite environmental condition score
raw_response.population_and_sample: 758 segregated habitats (colonies of at least four lower-quality dwelling units) containing approximately 134,000 inhabitants (low estimate 133,072; high estimate 134,320; 94% of colonies populated predominantly by Roma) identified across all 3,145 settlements in 19 counties of Hungary (excluding Budapest). Unit of analysis: colony (segregated part of settlement) and county.
raw_response.rationale: This empirical nationwide environmental survey maps 758 segregated Roma colonies across 19 Hungarian counties and reports colony-level lack of piped water mains and lack of sewerage/drainage (satisfying C1, C3, C4, and C6). However, it is a descriptive environmental and demographic mapping study focused on participatory minority research methodology, colony population estimation (versus census ethnic self-identification), and composite environmental deprivation scoring. It does not examine any legal, administrative, institutional, regulatory, or governance factor—under either the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type mechanism scope or the plain wording of Criterion 2—as an exposure governing water or sanitation service access. Excluded under E03 (Wrong exposure).
